drivingQuestion: How much separation between meat and cheese does the concern that they be eaten together require?
outcomeNote: The mishna records a rule and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel's clause; nothing is argued out here.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ צוֹרֵר אָדָם בָּשָׂר וּגְבִינָה בְּמִטְפַּחַת אַחַת, וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ נוֹגְעִין זֶה בָּזֶה. רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵי אַכְסְנָאִין אוֹכְלִין עַל שֻׁלְחָן אֶחָד, זֶה בָּשָׂר וְזֶה גְּבִינָה, וְאֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «A person may bind meat and cheese in one cloth, provided that they do not come into contact with each other. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: Two» unacquainted «guests [akhsena’in] may eat» together «on one table, this» one eating «meat and that» one eating «cheese, and they» need «not be concerned» lest they come to violate the prohibition of eating meat and milk by partaking of the food of the other.

moves.cueHe: צורר אדם בשר וגבינה במטפחת אחת
moves.summary: meat and cheese may be wrapped in one cloth provided they do not touch
moves.about: how far the concern that meat and cheese will come together reaches — the first tanna guards even two foods lying in one cloth, while Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel is unconcerned about two strangers eating meat and cheese at one table

moves.summary: two unacquainted guests may eat meat and cheese at one table without concern
